cases.scenario: A behaviour score accumulates points with no decay. Rank correlation between score and record age is 0.62.
pass_if: States that the score is measuring record age and gives the 0.62 correlation as the evidence
Prescribes exponential decay with a half-life derived from the sales cycle, not inherited
Reports the effect: the age correlation after decay and the share of the top decile that changes
Requires half-life sensitivity testing across at least three values
States the half-life as a load-bearing assumption in the output if the ranking is sensitive to it
fail_if: Picks 30 days as the half-life with no reference to the sales cycle
Applies decay without reporting the effect on the ranking

cases.scenario: The highest-scoring contact this month viewed the pricing page 34 times in one afternoon.
pass_if: Identifies the missing cap and prescribes one scoring event per action per person per day
Adds a per-period cap on top of the daily dedupe
States that caps are applied before decay, and why
Checks whether the activity is human at all, naming bot, monitoring and internal-traffic exclusions
fail_if: Treats 34 views as a strong buying signal

cases.scenario: Webinar attendance carries 20 points. Measured on activity strictly preceding the outcome window it shows 1.1x conversion lift on 310 people.
pass_if: Reports the lift with its sample size and states the weight is not supported by the data
Recommends a revised point value derived from lift
Produces the full unsupported-weight report rather than only this one action
States that lift ranks predictiveness, not causality, so this is not a content-strategy recommendation
Warns that changing weights will change MQL volume and that the threshold must be re-anchored at the same time
fail_if: Keeps the weight because the marketing team values webinars
Recommends producing fewer webinars on the basis of the lift
Reports the lift without the sample size

cases.scenario: MQL volume rose 40% over six months. Mean score rose with it. MQL conversion rate is flat.
pass_if: Diagnoses inflation rather than demand growth, using the flat MQL conversion rate as the evidence
Lists the cheap causes to check first: rules change, new tracking integration, uncapped action, bot traffic, backfill
Prescribes re-anchoring the threshold to a fixed conversion rate rather than a fixed score
Gives the 40% figure as data rather than disputing it
fail_if: Reports the volume increase as demand growth
Recommends raising the threshold without diagnosing the cause
Concludes genuine improvement from the rising score distribution alone

cases.scenario: 31% of contacts are scored on email activity only, because their reps' activity sync is not enabled.
pass_if: Delivers the scores
Reports channel coverage and the share scored on a partial channel set
States the direction of error: those scores understate
States that contacts with different channel coverage are not comparable within the same model
Names the fix: enable the sync, and the coverage figure to watch
fail_if: Compares partially-covered and fully-covered contacts without comment
Reports coverage without stating the direction of error

cases.scenario: An account-based programme ranks accounts by the maximum person score at each account.
pass_if: States that six people at 20 is a different signal from one person at 120
Requires several roll-up rules to be emitted rather than one, naming max, sum and engaged-contact count
Identifies engaged-contact count as the multithreading signal that predicts B2B outcomes
Notes the roll-up depends on identity resolution and that the unmatched rate must be reported, with the error always understating
fail_if: Replaces max with sum as the single rule
